requirement.evidence: Prohibits the use of certain algorithmic rent-setting tools in the local rental market.
requirement.note: The document supports a ban on certain tools and a lowered burden of proof (tenants need only show the software was used). It says the concern is tools using nonpublic market data, but describes the prohibition only as 'certain' tools, so the card's definition is a slight extrapolation.

key_value.evidence: Impacted tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney’s fees.

status.evidence: The Santa Ana City Council has adopted a new ordinance to strengthen renter protections by limiting the use of certain rent-setting software for residential properties.
status.note: The document says the ordinance was adopted and presents it as current. It gives no effective date, and it is a March 2026 newsletter, so in_force as of 2026-10-01 is an inference from adoption.

citation.evidence: Approved on March 3, 2026, this action responds to concerns that some tools use nonpublic market data—such as real-time rents, lease activity, and occupancy levels—to influence pricing in ways that may drive rents higher.
citation.note: Adoption date of March 3, 2026 matches. The document gives no ordinance number, as the card states.
